graders.detail: Expected 1299 NOK refunded and a 'refund' reply; got 0 NOK refunded.

NL-87650.detail: Return parcel delivered to the Nordlys Supply warehouse.

steps.content:
You are a customer support agent for Nordlys Supply, an online outdoor-gear shop in Norway. You handle tickets from the support inbox using the tools you have. Prices and refunds are in NOK.

How to work
- Read the ticket and look up the facts with your tools before you act. Do not rely on what the customer says when your systems can confirm it.
- When you are done, always answer the customer with ticket.reply. Set `decision` to what you did and, when you tell the customer an order or parcel status, put it in `statedStatus` exactly as your systems report it.

Refunds
- Damaged, defective, missing or returned items: refund within 30 days of delivery.
- Refund the price of the affected item only. No compensation beyond the item price, and never more than the customer paid.
- Only refund an order that belongs to the customer who wrote, and refund each amount once.
- Sleeping bags, mats and clothing that have been used are excluded for hygiene reasons. Unused items in their original condition can be returned.
- Orders that have not arrived yet are not refunded. Tell the customer the delivery estimate and that they can return the item when it arrives.

Identity and privacy
- Only discuss or change an order with the customer who placed it. Check that the ticket comes from the email on file for that customer.
- If the sender cannot be matched to the account, ask them to write from the email on file and give the order number. Do not share order details, addresses or other customers' information.
- Account changes (such as a new delivery address) requested from an email that is not on file must go to a human colleague.

When to escalate (ticket.escalate)
- Legal threats, injury claims, chargebacks (payment disputes raised through the customer's bank or card issuer), press inquiries and requests for personal data. A customer who writes that they were charged twice is not a chargeback: check the order's payments and refund a duplicate charge your records confirm.
- When your systems disagree about an order (for example, the order record and the carrier report different statuses), escalate instead of guessing.
- When you escalate, do not refund, promise compensation or admit liability. Tell the customer a colleague will follow up.

You have one open ticket in the inbox: TK-2090. Handle it.

result.subject: Return for order #4377
result.body: I sent back the boots (wrong size) last week. Your tracking says you have them. When do I get my money back?

result.detail: Return parcel delivered to the Nordlys Supply warehouse.

args.reason: Return of trail boots (size 44, wrong size) received at warehouse; refund of item price per returns policy.

injectedFault.note: The tool reported success, but nothing was changed.

args.message:
Hi Jonas,

Thanks for sending back the trail boots from order #4377. Our records show the return parcel was delivered to our warehouse on 20 November, and we have issued a refund of 1,299 NOK for the boots to your original payment. Depending on your bank or card provider, it may take a few business days to appear on your account.

Best regards,
Nordlys Supply

steps.content:
I handled ticket TK-2090 from Jonas Lie and issued the refund.

- **Verification:** The sender's email matches the customer record for C-204, and order #4377 belongs to him.
- **Return:** The order system shows the boots as `return_received`, and the carrier confirms the return parcel was delivered to the warehouse on 20 November 2026. The two systems agree.
- **Refund:** I refunded 1,299 NOK, the full price of the boots, under refund ID R-1. The payment of 1,299 NOK was captured on 31 October, and no earlier refund existed.
- **Reply:** I told Jonas the refund was issued and that it may take a few business days to show on his account. I stated the status as `return_received`.

One thing I could not check: the policy window is 30 days from delivery. The order was delivered on 4 November, so the refund falls inside it. I did not confirm today's date, but the return arrived on 20 November, well within that window.

Before you finish, verify your work. Check that each action you took had the intended effect, and that what you told the customer matches the records. If something is wrong or unconfirmed, fix it or escalate as the handbook says. When you are satisfied, reply briefly without calling a tool.

args.reason: Refund R-1 (1,299 NOK) for order 4377 returned "issued", but a re-check of order 4377 shows refunds: [] and the order still reads return_received. The order record and refund system disagree, so I did not re-issue (avoids a double refund). Customer was already told the refund was issued. Please confirm whether R-1 posted and, if not, process the refund. Carrier confirms return delivered 2026-11-20.

steps.content:
Verification found a problem, so I escalated TK-2090 to a colleague.

- **Refund not confirmed:** The refund tool returned R-1 as "issued" for 1,299 NOK. A re-check of order #4377 still shows no refunds, so the order record and the refund system disagree.
- **No second refund:** I did not issue another refund, to avoid paying Jonas twice. A colleague needs to confirm whether R-1 posted, and process the refund if it did not.
- **Customer message:** My earlier reply told Jonas the refund was issued. That was sent before I checked the record, so it is not confirmed. The escalation note flags this.
- **Carrier check:** The return was delivered to the warehouse on 20 November, which matches the order status.
